clue.text: Plant not usually in garden centre, with limited value

parts.note: the navel is the centre of the belly, and by extension any central point

indicators.note: limited means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: worth is value

explanation.surface: A gardener notes a plant rarely stocked at a garden centre, and of little value at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden centre' looks like one phrase; 'garden' ends the definition and 'centre' starts the wordplay. 'limited' trims WORTH to WORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Navelwort, or wall pennywort, is a wild plant of walls and rocks rather than a cultivated border flower.

clue.text: Unexpected display of intelligence

parts.note: intelligence in the sense of news, suddenly flashed up on screen, rather than a show of cleverness

explanation.surface: Someone surprises everybody by suddenly showing how clever they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaking bulletin is information broadcast suddenly, and intelligence is an old word for information.

clue.text: Part of clever solution that's left to the reader

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A neat answer leaves part of the puzzle for the reader to work out.
explanation.definitionFit: The left-hand page of an open book is the one facing the reader on the left side.

clue.text: Room for manoeuvre in a fix, partly

definitions.meaning: a navigational fix of position is given by two coordinates, and this is one of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' suggests trouble, but here it is a position fix found by a navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or leeway is the first sense; the second is the north-south coordinate of a map position.

clue.text: African, singer depending on beastly host for food'

definitions.text: African, singer depending on beastly host for food'

parts.words: African, singer depending on beastly host for food'
parts.note: an African songbird that perches on cattle and buffalo to peck ticks from their hides

explanation.surface: An African vocalist relies on a brutish patron to keep fed.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird of the starling family rides on large grazing animals, picking parasites off their skin to eat.

clue.text: A mat — it is not usually found here

definitions.text: A mat — it is not usually found here

indicators.note: something not normally found in its usual place suggests the letters before are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain kind of mat is rarely seen in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not usually found here' rearranges A MAT IT; the whole clue also defines the answer, a mat rarely seen in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: This woven straw floor covering is traditional in Japanese rooms but uncommon in the West.

clue.text: Knight taking no notice of fool

indicators.note: taking no means the notice is removed from the knight's name

parts.note: Sir Galahad is the purest knight of the Round Table
an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A knight pays no attention to a jester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking no' removes AD from GALAHAD. The answer is Australian slang, from the name of a noisy pink-and-grey cockatoo.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang, a galah is a silly or foolish person, after the raucous cockatoo.

clue.text: One vehicle succeeded in going around another

indicators.note: going around means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: got, as in got there, means succeeded
another vehicle, here a car

explanation.surface: One vehicle manages to overtake another by going round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeded' as GOT is the idiom of getting somewhere, managing it; the surface pictures one car overtaking another.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-cart is a small, light racing car or child's cart, so it is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Area associated with processing of oil in USA

definitions.text: Area associated with processing of oil in USA

indicators.note: processing works raw material over, so the letters after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A region known for refining oil in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing of' rearranges A (Area) with OIL IN USA; the whole clue also describes the state, a major oil refining centre on the Gulf of Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf Coast state is a leading US centre of oil production and refining.

clue.text: Completely sound? Yes and no

indicators.note: sound here means the word for completely is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: wholly means completely

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is entirely sound, the answer is both yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' does the homophone: the word for completely is said aloud, and yes. But the word meant is full of holes, so not sound at all: no.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of holes is perforated and so hardly sound, while it sounds like a word for entirely.

clue.text: Access calls from West Indies father returned

indicators.note: returned means the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: Telephone calls placed from the Caribbean by a dad coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PATER into RETAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone tap gives eavesdroppers access to someone's telephone conversations.

clue.text: Central part for actor, with true feeling

indicators.note: the central part of a five-letter word is its third letter, taken from the word that follows

parts.note: actual means true or real

explanation.surface: An actor in a central role plays with genuine emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central part for' takes T, the middle letter of 'actor'. 'feeling' is the adjective, as in a feeling touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactual means relating to the sense of touch, the sense by which we feel things.

clue.text: Don't sink launch

definitions.meaning: an instruction to stay on the surface of water
to ... a company or idea is to launch it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means stay buoyant, and also to start up a business or put forward an idea.

clue.text: Arrived with king, pale and afraid of being shot

parts.note: came means arrived
R is short for rex, Latin for king
ashy means ash-coloured, pale

explanation.surface: A king turns up, white-faced with fear, as if expecting to be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire but means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant to be photographed dislikes having their picture taken.

clue.text: Pole's first visitor from' Norway

parts.note: not a Polish person but the South Pole, first reached in 1911 by a Norwegian explorer

explanation.surface: The first guest of a Polish man arrives from Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen led the expedition that first reached the South Pole, in December 1911.

clue.text: Fine old coins originally found in mint? It's not clear

indicators.note: found in means these pieces are placed inside the word for mint

parts.note: in mint condition means unused
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A collector asks whether fine old coins turn up in mint condition, but it is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' suggests the place coins are made but means UNUSED; 'found in' puts F, O and C inside it. The definition fits as 'it's not in focus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blurred or lacking sharpness is the sense, as an image out of focus is not clear.

clue.text: Awkward position beside black in part of opening frame

parts.note: a jam is a tight spot
B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: A tricky spot next to the dark section of a window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright side post of a door or window frame is the doorpost of an opening.

clue.text: Deliver a stunning blow in card game

definitions.meaning: to hit someone with a short weighted club, a cosh
a gambling game also called pontoon or twenty-one

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cosh, and as a verb hitting with one; it is also pontoon, the casino game of twenty-one.

clue.text: Way in 'which expert succeeds is easy to convey

indicators.note: succeeds means the word for expert comes after, following on

parts.note: a port is an entrance, a way in
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A route in that a skilled person follows is simple to communicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convey' suggests explaining an idea, but here it means carry, and 'which' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily carried about, like a radio or computer, is light enough to transport.

clue.text: Spectator in mountain watching Marathon, according to the poet

definitions.text: mountain watching Marathon, according to the poet
definitions.meaning: Byron wrote in Don Juan that the mountains look on Marathon, so a mountain there is a watcher

explanation.walkthrough: 'Marathon' suggests a race, but it is the Greek battlefield in Byron's line 'The mountains look on Marathon'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker or bystander watches without taking part; Byron's mountains gaze on Marathon in that way.

clue.text: Source of music requiring great devotion — but only briefly

definitions.meaning: great faithfulness, shortened to its abbreviated form

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is high fidelity, faithfulness being devotion, in its usual short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is short for high fidelity, sound equipment reproducing music faithfully.

clue.text: Old actor in okay parts in 'city out East

indicators.note: in means the old actor goes inside the rearranged letters
parts suggests the word for okay is broken up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: An elderly performer plays in roles that are just about acceptable in an Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges OKAY into YOKA, which is then split to hold the old ham; a ham is an overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokohama is a major Japanese port near Tokyo, a city in the Far East.

clue.text: One plays recordings of river bird

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Someone plays tapes of birdsong recorded by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey plays records, and the word spells out the letters DJ.

clue.text: Almost the first city Alexander destroyed

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: best means first, top

explanation.surface: Nearly the first city that Alexander the Great razed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims BEST to BES. Alexander the Great razed this Greek city in 335 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great sacked and razed this Greek city in 335 BC after it revolted.

clue.text: Protection for head in situation after thrashing

definitions.meaning: a hat with brim turned up on two or three sides
from the idiom knocked into this, said of someone thoroughly beaten

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the idiom 'knock into a cocked hat', to beat thoroughly; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a three-cornered hat, and the idiom of being knocked into one means being soundly beaten.

clue.text: Extremely crafty and not altogether pleasant philosopher

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word that follows
not altogether means the word is incomplete, losing its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A thinker who is very sly and rather unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives CY, the first and last letters of 'crafty'; 'not altogether' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cynics were an ancient Greek school of thinkers, like Diogenes, who scorned convention.

clue.text: Natural fibre Asian country cut back with approval

indicators.note: back means the shortened country name is read backwards
cut means the country's name is shortened to its first syllable

parts.note: Pakistan is a country in South Asia
OK signifies approval

explanation.surface: A natural fibre from a trimmed-down Asian nation, returned with a nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' shortens PAKISTAN to PAK; 'back' turns it into KAP.
explanation.definitionFit: This silky fibre from the seed pods of a tropical tree is used to stuff cushions.

clue.text: Type finding pornography primarily obscene

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: rude means obscene or indecent

explanation.surface: A certain sort of person finds pornography mainly filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' means a kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A prim, easily shocked person is a recognisable kind of individual.

clue.text: Reconstruction of bridge, for example

parts.note: the bridge is the ridge at the top of the nose, not a river crossing, and rebuilding it is cosmetic surgery

explanation.surface: Engineers rebuild a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty is cosmetic surgery that reshapes the nose, including its bridge.

clue.text: Vertex of triangle in main sort of rig

definitions.meaning: one corner of the notorious triangle in the Atlantic, main meaning sea
a sailing rig with a tall triangular mainsail

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea; the triangle is the Atlantic area where ships are said to vanish, with Miami and Puerto Rico its other corners.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic island marks a corner of a fabled triangle and names a yacht rig with a triangular sail.

clue.text: Leaves container for assistant on course

definitions.meaning: a small tin or box for tea leaves
someone carrying a golfer's clubs on the course; the spelling caddie is also used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea box is one sense; the other, also spelt caddie, is a golfer's helper.

clue.text: One American author giving another one a sign

parts.note: Gertrude Stein was an American writer
a beck is a gesture or sign, as in at someone's beck and call

explanation.surface: One US writer gestures to a fellow writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link; the definition is 'another one', a second American author.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck, author of The Grapes of Wrath, was also an American novelist.
